findings.checklist_item: Acknowledge the prior art (MATTR / windowed type-token ratio, Covington & McFall 2010, and n-gram trajectory-repetition loop detection) and state why the single-trailing-window distinct-ratio was chosen over MATTR's window-averaged form and over subsequence-repetition detection, or adopt the established form.
evidence: Plan: 'Set-cardinality over a trailing window divided by the window size is order-insensitive ... and catches every cycle length' — this is the MATTR construction (windowed distinct/total, length-invariant).

Retrieved (conductscience.com/quanteda.io): MATTR from Covington & McFall (2010) averages distinct-types/window-size over sequential moving windows; adopted precisely because 'every window is the same length, the resulting average is invariant to how long the overall sample is — the single biggest criticism of traditional TTR disappears.'

Plan's own 'false-trip shape a whole-sequence denominator would have produced' independently restates TTR's known length-sensitivity flaw that MATTR was designed to fix — evidence the plan reinvents rather than references the pattern.

Retrieved (mbrenndoerfer.com agent-evaluation): established agent loop detection uses 'N-gram repetition: checking if specific action sequences repeat within a trajectory' — a complementary/alternative technique the plan does not consider.
The plan uses a SINGLE trailing window, not MATTR's average-over-all-windows; this divergence is unremarked, so the trade-off vs the canonical form is unexamined.
findings.finding: The plan's windowed distinct-ratio discriminator ('set cardinality of signatures over the trailing window divided by window size; order-insensitive; length-robust') is a rediscovery of the established Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR, Covington & McFall 2010) — the standard windowed distinct/total metric in computational linguistics — yet the plan cites no prior art and does not weigh its choice against MATTR or against n-gram/subsequence repetition detection, an established agent loop-detection technique that would identify the repeated cycle itself rather than only flag low diversity.
findings.location: Approach section and 'The shared discriminator contract' table
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why 24/0.50 constants were chosen and whether an established metric with published norms exists.
c827's actuator is later tuned and the team wants literature-backed thresholds rather than three hand-fit traces.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art' note to the Approach: name the windowed distinct-ratio as MATTR (Covington & McFall 2010) and n-gram trajectory-repetition (agent-eval practice); justify the single-trailing-window simplification (last-window responsiveness for a live actuator) versus MATTR's average, and note that a distinct-ratio flags low diversity while subsequence detection would name the cycle — keeping the ratio as the additive, order-insensitive signal but citing the lineage that grounds the 24/0.50 constants.
